decisions.reason: After two years on the market, this camera remains close to the firm's core offer and publicly committed strategy, so prior investment and reputational commitment make withdrawal unlikely.
This modular camera line strongly matches the firm's stated move toward compact and flexible sensors, and the existence of several models increases sunk costs and commitment to continue.

The sensor suite extends established capabilities into future spacecraft operations, and in a growing R&D-intensive setting management is likely to explain any shortfalls as temporary rather than exit.

Although it was only mentioned rather than prominently featured, the miniaturized space-qualified LiDAR sensor still fits the firm's technology base and miniaturization trajectory, so commitment remains stronger than any case for withdrawal.
The radiation-hard camera line was launched visibly in 2024 and sits squarely within the firm's heritage of reliable space imaging, making continued support highly likely.

This asteroid navigation and imaging camera is more niche and less visibly committed on the website, but it still builds on core competencies and management can plausibly treat early market uncertainty as temporary.
